title: Dapagliflozin vs placebo for cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure in HFmrEF/HFpEF
question: In adults with heart failure and mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction, does dapagliflozin reduce the composite of cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure versus placebo? (Double-blind placebo-controlled RCTs; HR estimand.)

withdrawn.summary: The result previously published on this page for its primary outcome was a cardiovascular-death-only registry measure served as the composite outcome. It is withdrawn.
statements: What was published: DELIVER (NCT03619213, PMID 36027570), HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.74 to 1.05), p=0.17 -- ClinicalTrials.gov measure 'Subjects Included in the Endpoint of Cardiovascular Death', a component of the composite, served as the review's k=1 primary result; a null-crossing conclusion.

What the held evidence holds: the registered PRIMARY composite (ClinicalTrials.gov measure #1, 'Subjects Included in the Composite Endpoint of CV Death, Hospitalization Due to Heart Failure or Urgent Visit Due to Heart Failure', all randomised patients, full analysis set) reports HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.73 to 0.92), p=0.0008. A second PRIMARY measure on the LVEF<60% subpopulation reports 0.83 (0.73 to 0.95). These are quoted as what the source holds; they are NOT stated here as this review's result.

Why: the declared component set for 'Composite cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure' was ['cardiovascular death'] -- the topic declared no components, so the target was the vocabulary's reading of the title -- and a cardiovascular-death-only registry measure matched a cardiovascular-death target with missing_components empty and was classified EXACT_TARGET. A wrong target, matched faithfully.
The correct result was in the held registry data (cache/dapagliflozin-hfpef-hosp/records.json, ctgov_results) throughout.

The corrected estimate is not yet published: registry analysis selection by identity (registered analysis set, never array order; a stated subpopulation is never the review's ITT result) and the confidence-level fix (the interval level travels with the analysis) must land first. Replacing a wrong number with a right number carrying a wrongly-labelled interval is not a correction.
Provenance: found by an independent verifier panel while measuring the cost of strict endpoint binding -- the rule refused this row, a true positive; confirmed against the ClinicalTrials.gov v2 API.
withdrawn.status: Pooled estimate withheld until the corrected selection is served with its own correction record.

comparator_scope_note: k=1 CONTRIBUTING, not a complete-evidence claim: DELIVER (NCT03619213) supplies the only EXTRACTABLE primary-outcome estimate here. This is NOT a claim that the eligible evidence base is a single trial -- 5 records screened in for this PICO and 4 are declared absent for this pooled number (no extractable primary estimate in the committed source). External audit also flagged further eligible HFpEF records (e.g. an EMPA-VISION-style cohort design) that a trial-level search can miss; the concept-query search rebuild is the fix. The nearest published synthesis pools the SGLT2-inhibitor CLASS (a broader, network-level PICO), so its larger k is a scope difference, not evidence this review failed to retrieve.
